summary: Lewis & Clark NF 50-foot pole L-4 tower dated to 1935; sources disagree on whether it was destroyed in 1968 or removed, and none describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Firelookout.com says destroyed in 1968; a Forest Lookouts page says removed

events.note: Dated 1935 by firelookout.com: 50-foot pole L-4 tower
Firelookout.com says destroyed in 1968; the Forest Lookouts page says removed and gives no date

evidence.supports: about nine miles NNE of Neihart
Lewis & Clark National Forest is listed as its agency
Forest Lookouts page lists the tower as removed
listed as a tower with status Gone, at 47.06590 north and 110.60412 west
evidence.quote: Anderson Peak Judith Basin 47.06590 -110.60412 Tower Gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com gives a destroyed date of 1968; the Forest Lookouts page says only Removed, with no date. The story reports both and does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: Two descriptive sources, both agreeing on location, agency and the 1935 tower but disagreeing on the fate (destroyed in 1968 versus removed, undated). The 1968 date appears only on firelookout.com. Staffing and access are not in any source. The Forest Lookouts page carries no date or narrative beyond the status line and location code. Search results also returned a different Anderson Peak lookout in California on firetower.org; it is not this site and was ignored. Brief record checked: county, agency, kind (tower) and coordinates match the sources.
